text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/01/07 - Essay - 01
People share a meal and conversation.
Pexels · 9220890
Around the table
There is more than one way to share a meal. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful starting
points.
One reason is that a simple plan leaves time for conversation. For instance, we prepare the vegetables before our guests arrive. This
prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that sharing the work helps everyone feel included. For example, each guest brings one dish and helps clear the
table. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different
things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Write guidance for someone who wants to share a meal for the first time. Explain two useful choices and why they matter. Use four
short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss a
simple plan leaves time for conversation with an example; discuss sharing the work helps everyone feel included with a different
example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
